title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Permissive vs. Mandatory Withdrawal
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: Which of the following scenarios describes a situation where a paralegal **may** withdraw from representation (permissive withdrawal) rather than being **required** to withdraw (mandatory withdrawal)?
options: The paralegal discovers they lack the competence to handle the specific area of law.
The client instructs the paralegal to lie to a tribunal adjudicator.
The client repeatedly fails to pay the paralegal's agreed-upon retainer fees despite reasonable notice.
The client discharges the paralegal in writing.
questions.explain: Under Rule 8.02, non-payment of fees is a ground for permissive withdrawal (the paralegal *may* withdraw), provided that the withdrawal does not result in serious prejudice to the client. Lack of competence, being discharged by the client, and being instructed to violate the Rules of Conduct trigger *mandatory* withdrawal.
